discarded_findings_note: 4 findings discarded as outside FGC core practice areas: Swiss Federal Council Banking Act/TBTF reform (bank capital regulation, not wealth management advisory); Jersey Basel III prudential rules for banks (effective 2027, bank capital regulation); Guernsey Finance Sector Concierge and US Qualified Jurisdiction application (market development news, not client compliance obligations); Brazil BCB VASP authorization deadline (regulatory licensing for crypto service provider businesses, not HNW client obligations).

findings.title: Luxembourg subscription tax filing transition period ends TODAY — MyGuichet mandatory from September 1, 2026
findings.summary: The two-year transition period for Luxembourg subscription tax filings ends August 31, 2026. From September 1, 2026, use of the new MyGuichet filing forms becomes mandatory for UCIs, SIFs, and RAIFs. Filers must now provide additional data, and CSSF/ISIN identifiers for RAIF compartments are required. The AED will also systematically issue subscription tax account statements.
findings.client_impact: Clients holding interests in Luxembourg UCIs, SIFs, or RAIFs — or fund managers running such structures — must ensure their Luxembourg fund administrators have transitioned to the new MyGuichet forms immediately, as any filing submitted via legacy forms from tomorrow onward will be non-compliant. Failure to update creates tax compliance risk at the fund level that can affect investor reporting and distributions.
findings.urgency_reason: URGENT: The deadline is today, August 31, 2026. The new mandatory filing format takes effect tomorrow. Any Luxembourg fund clients or advisors not yet transitioned must act immediately or face non-compliance.

findings.title: Cayman Islands new AML Rule and Sanctions Rule effective September 18, 2026 — 18 days
findings.summary: CIMA published a new Rule on Effective Compliance Programme for Prevention and Detection of Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Proliferation Financing, and a new Sanctions Rule on Compliance with Financial Sanctions. Both rules enter into force September 18, 2026, and apply to all CIMA-registered or licensed entities including registered investment funds.
findings.client_impact: Clients who are directors, general partners, or managers of Cayman-registered investment funds must ensure their fund's compliance programme is upgraded to meet the expanded CIMA AML Rule requirements before September 18 — this includes reviewing and updating AML policies, procedures, and sanctions screening protocols. Funds that fail to have a compliant programme in place on September 18 face CIMA regulatory action.
findings.urgency_reason: URGENT: Effective date is September 18, 2026 — 18 days from today. All CIMA-regulated entities (including registered funds) must be compliant on that date. Compliance programmes must be reviewed and updated now.

findings.title: US estate and gift tax exemption permanently raised to $15M per person — major wealth planning recalibration underway
findings.summary: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed July 4, 2025) raised the federal estate and gift tax exemption to $15 million per person ($30M per married couple with portability) effective January 1, 2026, with annual inflation adjustments from 2027. The prior law sunset — which would have cut the exemption to ~$7M in 2026 — is permanently eliminated. The annual gift exclusion remains at $19,000 per donee.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients who deferred large lifetime gifts or trust funding pending the sunset should revisit their estate plans now to take advantage of the permanently elevated $15M exemption; clients with irrevocable trusts or gift programs sized for a $7M world may need restructuring. The certainty of the permanent exemption also reopens grantor trust, dynasty trust, and intra-family loan strategies that were deprioritized during the sunset uncertainty.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: Already effective January 1, 2026, but the permanence of the high exemption creates ongoing and time-sensitive planning opportunities for HNW clients — particularly those who did not act in 2024-2025. Estate plans established under the old sunset assumption should be reviewed as a priority.

findings.title: CRS 2.0 — first major Common Reporting Standard update since 2016 now in effect, expanded reporting scope for 2026 cycle
findings.summary: CRS 2.0 entered into effect from January 2026, the first major update to the Common Reporting Standard since its 2016 adoption. Key changes include an expanded scope of reportable assets and strengthened due diligence requirements. Financial institutions in participating jurisdictions must implement enhanced reporting obligations for the 2026 reporting cycle.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients with offshore accounts, foreign investment entities, or structures in CRS-participating jurisdictions will be subject to expanded automatic reporting to their home tax authority for the 2026 cycle — potentially including asset classes not previously reportable. Clients should review their offshore structures for CRS 2.0 compliance and ensure their financial institutions have updated their due diligence processes.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: Already in effect, but financial institutions are actively implementing enhanced reporting and due diligence for the 2026 cycle. Clients need to understand the expanded scope before year-end to ensure correct disclosures and avoid unexpected tax authority inquiries.

findings.title: UAE Capital Market Authority (formerly SCA) — 12-month market participant transition period ends December 31, 2026
findings.summary: Federal Decree-Laws No. 32 and 33 of 2025 reconstituted the SCA as the Capital Market Authority from January 1, 2026, introducing a statutory prospectus liability regime, safe harbor for price stabilization, higher penalties, a recovery and resolution regime, and CMA authority over virtual asset trading. Market participants have until December 31, 2026 to comply.
findings.client_impact: Clients holding UAE-listed securities, participating in UAE capital market transactions, or using UAE structures for virtual asset trading must review their documentation and disclosure practices under the new CMA framework before year-end. The significantly increased penalties under the new law mean non-compliance carries materially higher financial risk than under the old SCA regime.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: Transition deadline is December 31, 2026 — four months from today. Clients with UAE capital market exposure need a compliance gap review before Q4, as the penalty regime has materially increased.

findings.title: BCB Resolution 575 expands foreign currency deposit account eligibility — effective October 1, 2026
findings.summary: The Central Bank of Brazil enacted Resolution No. 575 on June 18, 2026, expanding the categories of legal entities eligible to hold foreign currency deposit accounts in Brazil. The regulation takes effect October 1, 2026, as part of Brazil's continuing foreign exchange liberalization under the 2021 Foreign Exchange Law framework.
findings.client_impact: Brazilian HNW clients who hold or direct corporate entities previously ineligible to maintain foreign currency accounts in Brazil should assess whether their entities now qualify under the expanded rules — this could simplify FX management and international payment flows without requiring offshore structures. Wealth advisors should coordinate with Brazilian counsel to map eligible entity types before October 1.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: Effective October 1, 2026 — 31 days from today, effectively a one-month action window. Clients who may benefit from the expanded FX account eligibility should begin the analysis and account-opening process now, as Brazilian bank onboarding can take several weeks.

findings.title: Cayman Islands Q2 2026 CIMA regulatory update — substance requirements, fund governance, and AML Rule preparation
findings.summary: The Waystone Q2 2026 update covers CIMA enforcement actions, ongoing fund governance obligations, substance requirements for investment funds, and CIMA examination priorities. The interplay between the new AML Rule (effective September 18, 2026) and fund registration obligations is a key focus area.
findings.client_impact: Clients who are directors or managers of Cayman funds should confirm that their substance requirements are being met and that their compliance programmes are being updated ahead of the September 18 AML Rule deadline; CIMA is actively conducting examinations and enforcement actions, raising the risk of scrutiny for under-resourced fund governance arrangements.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: CIMA examinations and enforcement are active; the linked AML Rule (September 18) makes this time-sensitive. Fund governance gaps identified now can still be remediated before the new rule takes effect.

findings.title: FINMA major AML Ordinance update 2026 — enhanced UBO transparency and risk-based supervision for external asset managers
findings.summary: FINMA is implementing a major update to its Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance in 2026, focusing on beneficial ownership transparency aligned with FATF recommendations and EU AML directives. External asset managers and other financial intermediaries face enhanced due diligence obligations for identifying and verifying ultimate beneficial owners.
findings.client_impact: Clients using Swiss-regulated external asset managers or Swiss financial intermediaries should expect enhanced UBO identification and verification requests as their service providers implement the updated FINMA AML Ordinance; clients with complex ownership structures or nominee arrangements in Swiss-managed accounts may face additional documentation requirements.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: Implementation is underway in 2026 with no single public deadline confirmed, but FINMA supervision is active and financial intermediaries are adjusting their onboarding and monitoring frameworks now. Clients should anticipate requests for updated UBO documentation.

findings.title: Singapore MAS introduces tax exemption for fund management profit-related returns and ONE Pass Investment Management Track
findings.summary: On August 19, 2026, MAS announced a new tax exemption for profit-related returns from fund management services to qualifying funds under Sections 13D, 13O, 13OA, 13U, and 13V of the Singapore Income Tax Act, expected effective from Year of Assessment 2027. A dedicated Investment Management Track under the ONE Pass framework was also launched to attract global investment professionals.
findings.client_impact: Clients who manage or invest in Singapore-based qualifying funds should review whether their fund structures are eligible for the new carried-interest-style tax exemption from YA 2027, potentially increasing after-tax returns for fund managers; the ONE Pass Investment Management Track may also interest clients considering relocating to Singapore as a family office or investment management hub.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: Expected effective from YA 2027; final implementing legislation and eligibility details are still pending. Clients with Singapore fund structures or relocation plans should monitor closely and engage Singapore advisors to assess qualification.

findings.title: DIFC and ADGM intensify AML compliance in 2026 — enhanced CDD, digital assets, and tokenisation consultations ongoing
findings.summary: DIFC and ADGM regulators are prioritizing enhanced AML compliance in 2026, with stronger CDD requirements, risk assessments, and transaction monitoring. Both free zones are actively consulting on digital asset and FIAT-referenced tokenisation frameworks. DFSA Innovation Testing Licence and FSRA RegLab provide sandbox pathways for fintech.
findings.client_impact: Clients with entities or accounts in DIFC or ADGM should expect enhanced CDD and transaction monitoring from their DIFC/ADGM-regulated service providers; clients exploring digital asset structures in the UAE should engage early with the ongoing tokenisation consultations to shape structures that will remain compliant under the emerging frameworks.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: Ongoing regulatory intensification with consultations active — no single hard deadline, but non-compliance with enhanced CDD is an active examination risk. Digital asset clients should track consultation outcomes closely.

findings.title: Bahamas Draft Securities Industry Regulations 2026 open for consultation — Usufruct Interest Act 2026 also notable
findings.summary: The Securities Commission of The Bahamas has published Draft Securities Industry Regulations 2026 for public consultation, proposing to repeal and replace the 2012 regulations. Additionally, the Usufruct Interest Act 2026 introduces new wealth structuring legislation for the Bahamas.
findings.client_impact: Clients with Bahamas-registered funds or investment structures should have their Bahamas advisors review and respond to the consultation, as the new regulations may alter registration, governance, or reporting obligations; the Usufruct Interest Act 2026 may offer new structuring options for succession planning that FGC should evaluate for relevant clients.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: Consultation phase — no immediate compliance deadline, but the proposed regulations could materially change fund obligations once enacted. Clients should engage now to influence the outcome and prepare for transition.

findings.title: FinCEN permanently eliminates BOI reporting requirements for U.S. companies and U.S. persons — effective August 14, 2026
findings.summary: On August 11, 2026, FinCEN issued a final rule permanently removing the requirement for U.S. companies and U.S. persons to report beneficial ownership information under the Corporate Transparency Act. Effective August 14, 2026, U.S. companies no longer must file BOI reports and U.S.-person beneficial owner data is being deleted from the FinCEN database. Foreign entities that are reporting companies must still report BOI for their foreign individual beneficial owners.
findings.client_impact: U.S.-formed entities (LLCs, corporations, LPs, etc.) owned by U.S.-person clients no longer have any CTA BOI filing obligation, and previously submitted U.S. person data will be purged by February 10, 2027; however, clients with foreign-formed entities that are U.S. reporting companies (e.g., a foreign company registered to do business in the U.S.) must still report BOI for their non-U.S. individual beneficial owners.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: The rule has already taken effect (August 14, 2026) and eliminates a compliance burden rather than creating one. No client action is required for U.S. entities, but awareness of the foreign-entity carve-out is important for clients with mixed domestic/international structures.

findings.title: FinCEN BOI final rule in Federal Register — U.S. person data deletion cutoff February 10, 2027
findings.summary: The Federal Register published the final BOI Reporting Requirement Revision (Doc. 2026-16576) on August 14, 2026. The rule exempts reporting companies from filing BOI reports for U.S.-person beneficial owners and company applicants, and relieves U.S. persons from updating or correcting previously submitted data. FinCEN will delete all previously reported U.S. person BOI data with a cutoff of February 10, 2027.
findings.client_impact: Clients who previously filed BOI reports containing U.S.-person beneficial owner information can confirm that FinCEN will delete that data by February 10, 2027, removing the associated data-breach and disclosure risk from the federal registry. Clients with pending BOI corrections or updates for U.S. persons are now relieved of that obligation entirely.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: Supplements the FinCEN announcement — adds the specific data-deletion cutoff date of February 10, 2027. No client action required; this is background confirmation of the rule's implementation mechanics.

findings.title: Cayman Islands tokenised fund framework in force from March 24, 2026 — legal certainty for digital-token fund interests
findings.summary: The Private Funds (Amendment) Act 2026, Mutual Funds (Amendment) Act 2026, and Virtual Asset (Service Providers) (Amendment) Act 2026 came into force March 24, 2026, establishing a legal framework for tokenised funds. Fund operators must confirm annually to CIMA that digital token records are properly maintained, and token interest transfers require operator approval per the offering document.
findings.client_impact: Clients invested in or managing Cayman funds that have issued or plan to issue tokenised interests now have a clear regulatory framework to rely on, removing prior legal uncertainty; existing tokenised Cayman funds should confirm their annual CIMA confirmation obligations and ensure transfer restriction language in offering documents is compliant.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: Already in force since March 2026. Background awareness for clients with Cayman fund interests or tokenisation plans; no immediate deadline.

findings.title: BVI 'legitimate interest' access to beneficial ownership registers — effective April 1, 2026
findings.summary: Effective April 1, 2026, persons and institutions with a demonstrated 'legitimate interest' (regulatory, investigative, or otherwise) may apply for access to BVI beneficial ownership register data. Law enforcement retains direct access. The compliance deadline for existing BVI companies to file their beneficial ownership registers was January 1, 2026.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients with BVI entities should be aware that their beneficial ownership information is now potentially accessible to third parties with a claimed legitimate interest — not just law enforcement — which narrows the practical privacy protection of BVI structures compared to pre-2026; clients with genuine confidentiality concerns (e.g., safety risks, business sensitivity) should evaluate whether a formal exemption application is appropriate.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: Already effective since April 1, 2026. Background awareness for clients with BVI structures; the privacy landscape has materially changed and client structures should be reviewed in light of this.

findings.title: BVI beneficial ownership exemption applications available — protection for at-risk clients
findings.summary: From January 2, 2026, beneficial owners may apply to the BVI Registrar for exemptions from disclosure where disclosure could expose them or family members to fraud, kidnapping, extortion, harassment, or violence; where the beneficial owner is a minor or lacks capacity; where national security concerns arise; or where the Registrar determines disclosure is not in the public interest.
findings.client_impact: Clients who are prominent business figures, political figures, or face genuine personal safety risks should consider applying for a BVI beneficial ownership exemption to prevent their information from appearing in the accessible register; FGC should proactively identify clients in this category and engage BVI counsel to assess eligibility.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: Available since January 2026 with no deadline — this is an ongoing protection mechanism. However, given the April 1, 2026 opening of 'legitimate interest' access, at-risk clients who have not applied for exemption should be prioritized.

findings.title: Luxembourg revised carried interest regime — permanent statutory framework effective January 1, 2026
findings.summary: Luxembourg's Law of January 22, 2026 introduced a revised carried interest regime, retroactive to January 1, 2026, replacing prior administrative guidance with a clear and permanent statutory framework aimed at increasing Luxembourg's attractiveness as a fund domicile.
findings.client_impact: Fund managers receiving carried interest through Luxembourg fund structures should review their arrangements against the new statutory framework to confirm continued favorable tax treatment; the greater legal certainty may also make Luxembourg an attractive consideration for restructuring carried interest arrangements currently domiciled elsewhere.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: Already in force since January 2026. No immediate deadline; background awareness for fund manager clients with Luxembourg structures.

findings.title: OECD Pillar Two — first GloBE Information Return filings due June 30, 2026; US opts out; Qatar activates registration
findings.summary: First GloBE Information Return (GIR) filings for FY2024 were due June 30, 2026. The US announced in January 2026 it will exempt US-headquartered companies from Pillar Two and will not implement the framework. Qatar activated its GloBE registration service in August 2026 via Dhareeba. Approximately 140 countries have adopted the framework.
findings.client_impact: Clients with multinational group structures headquartered outside the US in Pillar Two-adopting jurisdictions should confirm their GIR filings were submitted by June 30, 2026, or that they qualify for transitional safe harbors; US-headquartered groups are exempt from Pillar Two obligations, which may affect the comparative attractiveness of US vs. non-US holding structures.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: First filing deadline has passed (June 30, 2026). Background awareness of the evolving global landscape, including the US opt-out and Qatar activation, which affects multi-jurisdictional planning for HNW clients.

findings.title: MFSA Financial Crime Compliance Strategy 2026 — risk-based supervision across funds, trustees, and CSPs
findings.summary: The Malta Financial Services Authority published its Financial Crime Compliance Strategy 2026 on August 5, 2026, centering AML prevention in its supervisory direction. The strategy introduces six pillars for stronger AML supervision, operational control testing, and EU AML alignment, directing resources toward higher-risk sectors including investment businesses, funds, insurers, trustees, and company service providers.
findings.client_impact: Clients using Malta-licensed trustees, fund administrators, or company service providers should expect enhanced AML due diligence requests and potentially increased scrutiny of their Malta-based structures as MFSA sharpens its risk-based supervisory focus; trustees and CSPs may impose higher compliance costs, which may feed through to client fees.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: Strategic direction published — no single hard deadline for clients, but supervisory intensity will increase throughout 2026 and beyond. Background awareness for clients with Malta structures.

findings.title: Cyprus tax reform effective January 1, 2026 — CIT raised to 15%, SDC cut to 5%, deemed dividend distribution abolished
findings.summary: Cyprus's comprehensive tax reform raised corporate income tax from 12.5% to 15% to align with Pillar Two. The Special Defence Contribution on dividends was reduced from 17% to 5% for actual distributions, and the deemed dividend distribution regime for post-2026 profits is abolished. Loss carry-forward extended to 7 years; R&D super-deduction extended through 2030; Tax Commissioner now has six-year asset statement and banking records access powers.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients using Cyprus holding companies or operating structures must update their tax models to reflect the higher 15% CIT rate, but the abolition of DDD and reduction of dividend SDC to 5% materially improves the effective tax rate on profit distribution — this may prompt a review of dividend policy and repatriation strategies for Cyprus structures. The enhanced Tax Commissioner audit powers warrant a review of historical transaction documentation.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: Already effective since January 1, 2026. Important background for all clients with Cyprus structures; retrospective analysis of 2026 income under the new rules should be underway with Cyprus advisors.

findings.title: Panama Superintendency of Banks Agreement 1-2026 — enhanced UBO identification at 25% and 10% thresholds
findings.summary: Panama's Superintendency of Banks issued Agreement 1-2026, requiring identification and verification of all UBOs holding 25% or more (with certified passport copies and proof of address), and broadening due diligence to identify individuals with 10% or more ownership or effective control. Digital ID verification and inferential geolocation were also introduced, aligning Panama more closely with FATF recommendations.
findings.client_impact: Clients with Panama banking relationships — including accounts held through Panama entities or trusts — should expect enhanced UBO identification requests from their Panamanian banks, including certified identity documents; clients who exercise effective control of an entity without holding a 25% threshold interest may now be identifiable and reportable under the new 'effective control' prong.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: Already effective from January 2026. Background awareness for clients with Panama bank accounts or corporate structures; documentation requests from Panama banks will likely increase throughout the year.

findings.title: Brazil Lei Complementar 227/2026 — progressive ITCMD nationwide, foreign assets and trusts explicitly taxable
findings.summary: Lei Complementar 227/2026 introduced mandatory progressive inheritance and gift tax (ITCMD) rates across all Brazilian states, shifting from flat book-value to market-value assessments. Foreign assets held by Brazilian tax residents are now explicitly subject to ITCMD, and foreign trusts face explicit ITCMD taxation. States may graduate rates up to 8% based on estate value.
findings.client_impact: Brazilian-resident HNW clients with foreign trusts, offshore investment accounts, or real estate abroad now face ITCMD at market value (up to 8%) on those assets at succession or gift — significantly increasing the cost of previously popular deferral structures and requiring immediate review of existing trust and estate plans with Brazilian tax counsel. Wealth planning strategy has shifted from offshore deferral to governance, asset protection, and coordinated Brazilian/foreign tax reporting.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: Already effective from January 2026. A critical and permanent structural change to Brazilian succession planning that every Brazilian-resident client with offshore assets must address; plans relying on the prior regime must be reviewed and likely restructured.

findings.title: Florida SB 264 foreign buyer restrictions upheld by Eleventh Circuit — near-total ban on Chinese nationals confirmed
findings.summary: On November 4, 2025, the Eleventh Circuit upheld Florida SB 264 (Shen v. Simpson), confirming the near-total ban on Chinese nationals purchasing Florida real estate and restrictions on nationals of Russia, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Venezuela, and Syria for agricultural land and property near military/critical infrastructure. A 2026 expansion to additional residential categories failed to pass the legislature. All buyers must sign compliance affidavits; violations carry forfeiture and criminal penalties.
findings.client_impact: Clients who are nationals or entities controlled by nationals of the seven restricted countries must continue to treat Florida real estate as effectively prohibited or severely restricted; the Eleventh Circuit ruling eliminates near-term federal litigation risk and makes the restrictions durable, so affected clients planning Florida real estate acquisitions should immediately redirect to non-Florida US markets or alternative structures not covered by SB 264.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: The law is upheld and settled. Background awareness for clients from restricted countries; no new action required for those already advised, but newly onboarded clients from those jurisdictions must be screened for Florida real estate plans.
